title: ms-per-token-claim-framework
content:
Purpose

Quick working framework for expressing "ms-per-token" style performance claims alongside unit-econ (cost/token) proof points for the sales and product GTM decks. Focus is on statements that are meaningful to engineering buyers (PLG and enterprise) and that we can validate/operate on. This is intentionally a light, testable claim matrix + suggested evidence collection plan.

Executive summary (1 paragraph)

Positioning we want: Redwood reduces tail latency and per-token serving cost simultaneously by combining runtime batching, quantization profiles, and smart routing. Framing: "ms-per-token" is a compact metric engineers understand — it maps directly to perceived responsiveness and to per-request compute cost. Goal: produce a short set of customer-facing claims (bold but verifiable) + an internal checklist to validate them in sales conversations.

Primary claim candidates (phrasing options)

- "Typical gen: 6–18 ms per token (p50–p95) for 2k context on open models with our default dedicated profile."
- "Up to 2x lower per-token inference cost vs. competing hosted endpoints on medium-length prompts (1–3k tokens) when using Redwood Optimize suggestions."
- "Consistent p95 tail: <100 ms on popular assistant flows with autoscaled dedicated pools and prefix caching enabled."

Note: these are draft numbers — exact language gated on bench validation and legal review.

Why ms-per-token works as a metric

- Intuitive mapping to UX (latency) and obvious mapping to CPU/GPU time (cost).
- Model- and workload-agnostic if we always publish configuration (model family, context length, batch size, quant profile).
- Easier to compare across vendors and across modes (hosted vs dedicated) when normalized for throughput and cache hit rate.

Proof inventory (what we have / rough status)

- Internal bench run: small-gen benchmark (open Llama-70B-8k-ish family quant-int8) on dedicated pool prototype. Observed p50 ~8 ms/token; p95 ~55 ms/token for 2k context, batch=4, kv-cache enabled. (raw logs: bench-id B-2025-02-04-8).
- Cost modeling spreadsheet (linked) showing per-1k-token cost at different batch sizes and quant levels (sheet: https://docs.google.com/sheets/d/benchmark-econ-2025).
- Field proof: 3 pilot customers on Dedicated reported perceived latency reduction in chat flows vs their previous self-hosted infra (qual notes in customer-stories doc).

Gaps / tests to run (priority order)

1) Controlled competitor head-to-head (must run before claim goes public):
   - Vendors to include: Vendor X (hosted endpoints), Vendor Y (managed dedicated service), Open self-host (customer-configured). Use identical model forks where possible (same quant, same hf weights).
   - Standardized workload: 2k context, 512-token generation, mixed instruction/control tokens, batch sizes {1,4,8}. Measure p50, p90, p95 ms/token and per-1k-token cost.
   - Regions: us-west1, eu-west1. Network overhead accounted separately.
2) Sensitivity table for caching: bench with/without prefix KV caching for conversational workloads to show delta on tail latency at p95.
3) End-to-end UX test with streaming enabled vs disabled (measure perceived time-to-first-token + tokens/sec).
4) Repeatability across model families (Llama-2-ish, Mistral-like, and an encoder-decoder sample) and quant modes (fp16, int8, int4 where available).

Bench methodology (short)

- Single-script harness (link in linked_artifacts) that: pins model weights, applies identical quant profile, warms KV cache for conversational runs, sweeps batch sizes, captures raw GPU / host metrics, and records latency histograms at token granularity.
- Run N=50 warmup, then N=500 measured sequences per config. Use bootstrap to compute CIs on p95.
- For cost: record GPU utilization and map to cost using current reserved capacity rates + incremental amortized overhead.

Competitor snapshot (quick notes from public docs / trials)

- Vendor X: advertises low-latency streaming. Our initial head-to-head showed similar p50 at small batch but p95 degrades rapidly under mixed traffic. Pricing: per-token starting higher on short sequences.
- Vendor Y: strong in single-model dedicated offering but limited quant/profile tuning; performs well at high throughput but at higher $/token at low to medium utilization.
- Open self-host: cheapest at scale but large ops overhead and often worse tail under bursty traffic without careful queueing.

Risk / compliance notes

- Avoid absolute superlatives ("fastest") — prefer "up to" and specify workload.
- All public claims must include test config footnote: model, context, batch, quant, region, caching.
- Legal/PR signoff required for any published numeric claim.

Sales cheat-sheet: quick soundbites and rebuttals

- Short pitch: "We measure latency in ms-per-token and design our stack to bring both the p95 and the $/1k-token down — so your chat UX is snappier and your unit-costs fall."
- Rebuttal: "If the prospect asks about real-world tails, offer to run a 48hr canary with their traffic into a dedicated pool and report p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens."

Sample customer-facing copy (for decks / one-pager)

- Headline: "Bring down latency and cost — measured per-token, verifiable by your traffic."
- Subhead: "Typical gen latency: single-digit to low-double-digit ms/token at p50; predictable p95 with cache-enabled Dedicated pools."

Claim guardrails (what to include with each claim)

- Exact model name + weight hash.
- Sequence length used + prompt distribution (samples).
- Batch size and concurrency.
- Quantization profile and runtime flags.
- Region and instance type, plus whether KV caching and streaming enabled.
- Link to bench run (artifact id).

Validation checklist before publication

- [ ] Head-to-head completed (bench artifact uploaded)
- [ ] Statistical significance for p95 (CI < 10% relative)
- [ ] Cost model updated (sheet version >= 2025-02-28)
- [ ] Legal/PR review queued (Confluence ticket referenced)
- [ ] Sales enablement blurb + sample scripts created

Next steps (owners & timeline)

- Run competitor head-to-head (Omar) — start 2025-03-06, 2 weeks
- Cache sensitivity runs + model family sweep (Aditi) — start 2025-03-06, 10 days
- Draft external claim wording + pull legal (Leah) — draft by 2025-03-14

Notes / freeform brainstorming

- Consider a simple ms-per-token badge for the Console that surfaces p50/p95 per-route — useful for sales screenshots.
- For enterprise pitch add a sentence on "predictable tails via routing and dedicated SLAs" — many infra buyers care more about predictability than absolute p50.
- Could add a customer case study: "Reduced median response time by 40% and cut cost/1k by 27%" — but must be verifiable before inclusion.

Unresolved questions

- Do we publish p95 for streaming-first experiences (we currently measure token emit latency differently)?
- How to normalize for compact prompt engineering (many customers aggressively shorten prompts and impact per-token measures).

End of doc.
